description: Stable, schema-backed registry of ALL agent-facing reason labels: the hard runtime blocker codes consumed by coordinator preflight (workspace_coordination_preflight), MCP dispatch (workspace_agent_dispatch), and launcher diagnostics, AND self-recoverable agent-facing nudge labels (e.g. the read_disclosure compact-read gate refusals) whose recovery is the caller re-calling with corrected arguments. This file is the sole canonical source of truth for the taxonomy: dispatch-specific consumers, launcher diagnostics, and the compact-read gate MUST select codes from this descriptor rather than inventing ad hoc strings. Codes are dimensioned by category and actor_recovery so a self-fixable nudge and a hard block can coexist in one enumerable list without a consumer mistaking one for the other; dispatch-facing projections filter to the dispatch/launch categories so nudge labels do not leak into the dispatch blocker catalog. BOOTSTRAP_STATE_CODES values are string-equal to the bootstrap entries below.

codes.summary: Caller role is forbidden from this action by the orchestrator/worker role policy.
codes.detail: Role policy is the orchestrator/coordinator/worker write-boundary contract: orchestrators may only edit docs/wiki coordination surfaces, workers must stay inside the assigned WK write_scope, reviewers/redteam must be findings-only. Use this code when the request is structurally outside the role's write-policy regardless of runtime state.
codes.consumer_notes: Dispatch admission and worker write-scope enforcement must use this code for policy violations; runtime filesystem failures must NOT collapse into this code. Structured reasons that ride on this code (e.g. reviewer_write_scope_nonempty) are listed under `reasons`; they are diagnostic context, not separate taxonomy codes.

reasons.summary: A reviewer dispatch named a subject whose selected slice or work-item declares a non-empty write_scope. Reviewers are findings-only and require write_scope: []. This reason rides as structured diagnostic context on role_policy_violation at the MCP dispatch admission boundary (workspace_agent_dispatch) and in the launcher reviewer role-plan paths (agent-role buildAgentRolePlan and the Codex read-only reviewer path); it is not a separate taxonomy code.

remediation.summary: The selected subject is shaped like implementation work, so it is the wrong subject for a findings-only reviewer. Create or select a separate review unit and dispatch the reviewer against that unit.
remediation.repo_paths: the implementation files the review inspects
acceptance: Report findings against the inspected files.

not_remediation: escalating or broadening filesystem write authority
invoking an operator role wrapper or direct CLI dispatch
adding prompt/env/argv/request identity or scope carriers

codes.summary: Caller/session role identity does not match the role required for the requested dispatch.
codes.detail: Use when the caller presents a launcher- or transport-minted identity that is valid but wrong for the target action (e.g., a worker session calls a coordinator-only dispatch surface).
codes.consumer_notes: Distinct from caller_supplied_identity: identity authority is valid, but the role does not match.

codes.summary: Identity was supplied through a non-authoritative carrier (request payload, prompt text, ambient env, argv, claimed_identity.role, docs inference).
codes.consumer_notes: CALLER_SUPPLIED_IDENTITY_CARRIERS owns the refused identity-carrier set. All carriers in that set must produce this code.

codes.summary: Target WK or slice is not independently executable (missing acceptance, validation, write_scope, docs, or evidence requirements).
codes.consumer_notes: Coordinator must revise the WK; implementation must NOT proceed against an unready record.

codes.summary: The restored managed-admission carrier does not match the current attempt, so managed dispatch fails closed before the worker spawns.
codes.detail: Use when the launcher-restored managed-admission carrier cannot be resolved or validated against the current attempt. The coordinator must re-derive and re-attest against the final carrier.
codes.consumer_notes: The emitted detail.issue is worker_admission_carrier_invalid; the nested detail.reason identifies the specific carrier failure.

reasons.summary: The canonical work-record digest changed after the attestation was recorded.
The canonical work record could not be resolved.
The provisioned worktree or binding does not match the carrier; orphan-state recovery is operator-side and tracked by WK-1568.
The launcher-frozen carrier could not be resolved.
The carrier failed revalidation before side effects.

codes.summary: Node Engine worker-admission needs review-threshold evidence; it is not a deny/reject result.
codes.detail: Use when a pack-backed worker-admission `needs_review` outcome reports `review_threshold_exceeded`. The normal recovery is to narrow or split the selected unit where possible, then record accepted review-attestation evidence for the selected unit/control, or use an operator-approved escalated implementation path if policy chooses it. DEC/ESC/accepted_authorities are separate policy or escalation authorities and are not proof that review was performed.
codes.consumer_notes: Dispatch and readiness projections should map this code to review-threshold recovery guidance while keeping selected unit, control, observed, and threshold facts in the dynamic pack-result projection rather than the static compact taxonomy surface.

codes.summary: Required structured/MCP transport for the requested action is not available in this session.
codes.consumer_notes: Used when the recommended MCP capability is not exposed by the active server. Agents must not fall back to shell role calls.

codes.summary: A required backend (filesystem MCP backend, registry, launcher daemon) is not reachable.
codes.consumer_notes: Distinct from missing transport: the structured transport exists, but its backing service or registry is not usable.

codes.summary: Implementation dispatch requires the managed lifecycle; unmanaged direct execution is not an implementation route.
codes.detail: Use when an implementation request is outside the server-owned managed lifecycle. This code does not imply that structured dispatch, native editing, repository reads, or commit are unavailable; each capability is reported independently by coordination preflight.
codes.consumer_notes: Recovery is a structured preflight followed by structured dispatch only. Consumers must not turn this blocker into caller-selected lifecycle configuration.

recovery.success_condition: managed lifecycle capability facts are fresh and the required planes report available

codes.summary: Managed implementation worktree provisioning is not currently available from the launcher-owned capability source.
codes.detail: Use when managed implementation dispatch cannot obtain a fresh, available provisioning fact. Provisioning absence, unknown authority, and stale authority all fail closed before worker spawn.
codes.consumer_notes: The operator restores the server-owned capability source; the coordinator rechecks it through the structured preflight route. No caller-provided provisioning values are accepted.

recovery.success_condition: managed_worktree_provisioning reports available from a fresh authoritative source

codes.summary: Mounted repository filesystem is read-only and required writes cannot be applied.
codes.detail: Reports a runtime filesystem fact, not a role-policy decision. Even when the orchestrator role policy restricts writes to docs/wiki, a failed write to one of those permitted surfaces is still a filesystem fact and MUST be reported with this code so operators can investigate the mount.
codes.consumer_notes: MUST NOT be reinterpreted as role_policy_violation.

codes.summary: Sandbox or container profile is denying writes the WK or coordination surface requires.
codes.detail: Use when the write denial is attributable to a sandbox/profile/seccomp rule rather than a misconfigured deploy mount. Resolution is operator-side sandbox/profile change.
codes.consumer_notes: Distinct from read_only_mount: the underlying filesystem accepts writes, but the sandbox profile rejects them.

codes.summary: The launcher-owned committed wiki-MCP runtime snapshot for a managed confined role could not be built or verified, so the role's authority-bearing MCP server would not start in-namespace.
codes.detail: WK-1555#SLICE-028 / DEC-0160 (staged-runtime successor). A managed confined Codex role executes the wiki-MCP server from a staged runtime built out of ONE immutable Git object snapshot of a launcher-owned committed revision: both member membership (git ls-tree at the commit) and file bytes (git cat-file) come from that revision, never from the index or the working tree. This code reports that the snapshot is not coherent and usable: the runtime source repository has no committed HEAD; a member is missing, non-regular (symlink/gitlink), or has an unreadable Git object; a runtime package has no tracked members at the frozen commit; a committed importer's target is not tracked at that commit or reaches a workspace package outside the tracked four-package superset; the staged directory is partial, corrupt, or conflicts with the requested (commit, digest) tuple; or the staged entrypoint is absent. The refusal is raised BEFORE role spawn and carries a bounded, repository-relative member diagnostic.
codes.consumer_notes: This replaces the former tracked-but-absent silent skip in codex-role-wiki-mcp-override.mjs. It MUST NOT be degraded to an opaque bwrap failure, an in-child module-resolution crash, optional-MCP behavior, or a later committed_slice_result_absent: the wiki-MCP server is the role's sole delivery (worker commit) or findings (reviewer/redteam) authority, so an incomplete runtime is a hard pre-spawn block. Recovery is operator-side: commit the launcher runtime source change (an uncommitted edit is deliberately not eligible), restore the missing object, or remove the conflicting staged directory. Distinct from managed_wiki_mcp_runtime_dependency_unavailable, which reports the dependency installation rather than the committed snapshot.

codes.summary: The owning repository's canonical node_modules installation that the staged wiki-MCP runtime links to is missing, redirected, malformed, or incompatible with the snapshot's committed manifests.
codes.detail: WK-1555#SLICE-028 / DEC-0160. The staged runtime provisions exactly one dependency link to the owning repository's canonical node_modules installation, which bwrap additionally binds read-only. Before use, the launcher verifies that the canonical target exists, is a directory, is not redirected away from the owning repository, carries npm's installed-tree marker, exposes the expected workspace aliases resolving back to the owning repository's packages, and satisfies every runtime dependency declared by the SNAPSHOT's committed package manifests. This code reports that one of those checks failed.
codes.consumer_notes: Scope note: this is ONLY the trusted staged runtime's dependency link. The general consuming-worktree <managed-worktree>/node_modules symlink is owned by agent-chassis:WK-1634 and is not provisioned under this code. Recovery is operator-side (reinstall or repair the canonical installation); it must never be worked around by widening the role's repository visibility or by allowing the role to launch without its MCP server.

codes.summary: Structured validation step (lint, work-record schema, closure schema, docs-policy) reported an error.
codes.consumer_notes: Diagnostics array carries the underlying validation findings.

codes.summary: Requested dispatch route (family/model/profile) is not supported.
codes.consumer_notes: Discovery exposes this route as deactivated/refusal-only/historical, or the family is not currently wired.

codes.summary: An agent-originating request attempted to use a non-MCP role route; the call is blocked and the agent must use MCP role dispatch.
codes.consumer_notes: MCP dispatch admission must emit this code when a non-MCP role route is reached by an agent caller.

codes.summary: Internal code reached a route that is hidden from agent-facing discovery; the request must fail closed without naming the hidden route.
codes.consumer_notes: Diagnostics must not leak the hidden route name to agent-facing output.

codes.summary: Agent-facing discovery surfaced a hidden route name; this is a discovery audience-scoping bug, not a normal blocker.
codes.consumer_notes: Reported during discovery audits; operator action is required to repair audience scoping.

codes.summary: MCP reviewer dispatch route (workspace_agent_dispatch --role reviewer) is not registered or not exposed in this session.
codes.consumer_notes: When MCP reviewer dispatch is unavailable in-session, implementation slices that are explicitly covered by the bootstrap review exception must use that exception instead of treating this as a hard close blocker.

codes.summary: MCP reviewer dispatch route exists but the runtime launch/monitor channel failed.
codes.consumer_notes: Distinct from mcp_reviewer_dispatch_missing: the route is shipped, but the current invocation cannot complete.

codes.summary: Mandatory findings-only review is required but no MCP reviewer route or authorized bootstrap exception is available.
codes.consumer_notes: Must not degrade to shell-launched review.

codes.summary: Dispatch monitor handle is unknown to the runtime; the handle does not correspond to a tracked role-run.
codes.consumer_notes: The monitor status path must emit this code instead of inventing a string.

codes.summary: Monitor handle is valid but refers to a different WK/slice subject than the request.
codes.consumer_notes: Detects cross-WK monitor-handle reuse.

codes.summary: Monitor handle is valid but the caller identity is not the launcher-minted owner of that run.
codes.consumer_notes: Detects cross-caller monitor-handle spoofing.

codes.summary: Monitor handle has already been consumed for a terminal status and is being replayed.
codes.consumer_notes: Monitor status handling must refuse replayed monitor handles.

codes.summary: Bootstrap review exception is active: MCP reviewer dispatch is unavailable in-session, and findings-only review evidence is recorded under the bootstrap path.
Bootstrap review exception requires findings-only review evidence before close, but none is recorded.
MCP reviewer dispatch has shipped; the bootstrap review exception is consumed for new work.
Graph impact is unavailable or errored: no usable base artifact and no usable dirty overlay.
codes.detail: Deterministic outcome for the unavailable/errors graph-impact sub-state. Operator must restore graph impact or the WK must mark graph-impact not applicable.
codes.consumer_notes: Covers graph_state=unavailable and graph_state=error.

codes.summary: Graph impact query itself errored even though the artifact appears present.
codes.consumer_notes: Distinct from graph_impact_unavailable: the artifact is present, but the query path raised.

codes.summary: Graph impact base artifact is missing (staleness=missing) and no usable dirty overlay covers it.
codes.consumer_notes: Operator refresh; agents must not rebuild in a dirty worktree.

codes.summary: Graph impact base artifact is stale or rebuild-required and no usable dirty worktree overlay is available.
codes.detail: Deterministic outcome for the stale/rebuild-required graph-impact sub-state. Operator must refresh; the worker must not rebuild inside a dirty worktree.

codes.summary: Graph impact proceeds using a dirty worktree overlay; degraded overlay evidence must be reported separately from canonical authority.
codes.detail: Deterministic outcome for the dirty-overlay sub-state. Non-blocking, but the dispatch result must surface the overlay evidence and the worker must record it in the WK closure.

codes.summary: Graph impact state could not be classified (staleness=unknown and no usable overlay).
codes.consumer_notes: Treated as a blocker until the operator restores a classifiable state.

codes.summary: Required graph-impact evidence cannot be persisted to the WK through MCP; shell/CLI persistence is not an allowed fallback.
The runtime blocker taxonomy descriptor itself could not be loaded; consumers must fail closed instead of guessing codes.
codes.consumer_notes: Reported when the descriptor file is missing, malformed, or unreadable.

codes.summary: Recovery is human/operator-only: the agent must stop and surface the recovery condition, not retry or escalate inline.
codes.consumer_notes: Use when the blocker requires operator action (registry reset, secret rotation, sandbox profile change, mount remount, drift fix) that no agent role is authorized to perform.

codes.summary: An expensive/verbose work-record read was attempted on a large unscoped record without a compact-first pass; do a compact read first (or supply a valid compact_read_token), then re-call.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry means the caller itself recovers by RE-CALLING with CORRECTED arguments (run the compact read first, or attach the compact_read_token it returns) -- this is NOT an identical retry, so WK-1502's identical-call loop cap must not miscount a corrected re-call. Emitted by the compact-read gate (work-record-compact-read-gate.mjs buildRefusal/buildReadRefusal) when validateToken reports a missing token on a large unscoped expensive request.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking and self-recoverable. Filtered OUT of the dispatch-facing blocker catalog (compactRuntimeBlockerTaxonomy) via RUNTIME_BLOCKER_DISPATCH_FACING_CATEGORIES.

codes.summary: No compact_read_token was supplied on a large unscoped expensive work-record read; obtain one from a prior compact read and re-call with it.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with CORRECTED arguments (attach the compact_read_token minted by the compact read), not an identical retry. Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate; buildRefusal maps this to compact_first_required on the refusal envelope.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: The supplied compact_read_token was not a well-formed bounded acknowledgment (undecodable, wrong shape or scalar types, wrong fixed lifetime, future-issued, or overlong); re-run the compact read to mint a fresh acknowledgment and re-call with it.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with the CORRECTED (freshly minted) acknowledgment, not an identical retry. The compact_read_token is a plain bounded base64url JSON acknowledgment used for stale-read / explicit-intent bookkeeping, so 'malformed' means the carrier was structurally invalid (undecodable, wrong field set, wrong scalar types, wrong fixed lifetime, future-issued, or overlong). Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: The compact_read_token schema_version does not match the expected compact-read token schema; mint a fresh token from a current compact read and re-call.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with a CORRECTED current-schema token, not an identical retry. Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: The compact_read_token was issued for a different tool family than the one being called; re-run the compact read for THIS tool to mint a matching token and re-call.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with a CORRECTED token minted for this tool family, not an identical retry. Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: The compact_read_token was issued for a different workspace repo or record id; re-run the compact read for the correct record and re-call with the corrected token.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with a CORRECTED in-scope token, not an identical retry. Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: The compact_read_token selector does not match the requested selector; re-run the compact read with the intended selector and re-call with the corrected token.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with a CORRECTED selector-matched token, not an identical retry. Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: The record changed since the compact_read_token was minted (source_digest mismatch); re-run the compact read to refresh the token against the current record and re-call.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with a CORRECTED token minted against the current source_digest, not an identical retry. Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: The compact_read_token TTL has elapsed; re-run the compact read to mint a fresh token and re-call with it.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with a CORRECTED (unexpired) token, not an identical retry. Emitted by validateToken in the compact-read gate.
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

codes.summary: Slice/record detail was omitted from the compact projection; re-call scoped to the specific selected_slice/selected_record to retrieve its detail.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with CORRECTED (narrowed) arguments naming the selected_slice or selected_record, not an identical retry. Emitted by the compact-read gate's bounded selected-slice/selected-read results (boundedSelectedSliceResult/boundedSelectedReadResult).
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog. Distinct from compact_read_selected_detail_required (which fires after a valid token is presented).

codes.summary: A valid compact_read_token was presented but the large unscoped expensive read stays bounded; re-call scoped to a specific selected_slice/selected_record instead of requesting the whole record.
codes.detail: actor_recovery=caller_retry: re-call with CORRECTED (narrowed) arguments naming the selected_slice or selected_record, not an identical retry. Emitted by the compact-read gate when validateToken accepts the token but the request is still large and unscoped (the refusalDecision branch). Distinct from selected_slice_compact_detail_required (the pre-token bounded-detail nudge).
codes.consumer_notes: read_disclosure nudge label: non-blocking, self-recoverable, excluded from the dispatch-facing blocker catalog.

graph_impact_state_map.description: Exhaustive deterministic mapping from (graph_state, staleness, dirty_state, overlay_state) to runtime blocker codes consumed by workspace_coordination_preflight and workspace_agent_dispatch readiness. The first matching rule wins. A null/unspecified field matches any value. WK-1590 current-HEAD ruling (2026-07-18, recorded on WK-1590): the graph baseline is derived from the current committed HEAD, so a stale, older-base, missing-overlay, or rebuild_required state is rebuilt at current HEAD rather than blocking -- staleness alone is never a blocking refusal. A valid dirty-worktree overlay is optional enrichment merged over the base (non-blocking graph_impact_degraded_overlay). Only a current-HEAD baseline that genuinely cannot be produced or validated (graph_state unavailable/error/query_error) is a zero-backend blocking refusal before CCE.
